messages:
sam: heads-up — p99 token latency on the token-slo dashboard spiked in apac-west around 03:06 UTC, correlates with a tokens/sec drop. https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/token-slo
anya: can you paste the panel link + time range? I want to see if GPU util moved too.
carmen: saw something similar earlier today in eu-west but smaller. might be NAT throttling again?
sam: panel: /d/token-slo?orgId=1&from=1670000000000&to=1670000100000&var-region=apac-west — p99 jumped from 180ms -> 640ms, tokens/sec dropped ~40%
mike: that pattern (tokens/sec down + latency up) usually means either network egress bottleneck or a downstream cache miss causing backpressure on runtime batching
luke: can we run the prom query for tokens/sec by node and NAT connections? quick ones: 
```
sum(rate(redwood_tokens_processed_total[1m])) by (node,region)
sum(redwood_nat_active_connections) by (node,region)
```
anya: also check GPU queue length and mz scheduler pending tasks: 
```
max(redwood_gpu_queue_depth{region="apac-west"}) by (node)
```
oncall-bot: (incident-meta) new alert fired: TokenSLO_p99_ApacWest (fired at 1769991175) severity=page
sam: thanks, oncall-bot — I ran those queries. NAT connections spiked on two frontends (fe-14, fe-15) and queue_depth on gpu-pool-3 rose briefly. GPU util stayed ~55% though. Looks like network tails not GPU saturation
carmen: any recent deploys to apac-frontends? deploy-bot shows no deploys in last 2 hours
mike: posting rough cost/latency correlate query so we can see cost-per-token drift during the event: 
```
(sum(increase(redwood_cost_cents_total[1h])) by (region) / sum(increase(redwood_tokens_processed_total[1h])) by (region))
```
anya: suggestion: add a small drilldown on the token-slo dashboard that joins these three panels (tokens/sec, nat_conn, gpu_queue) and pre-fills region filter. saves hunting during pages
luke: +1. also propose we change the alert to include a compound condition so it only pages when p99>500ms AND tokens/sec < baseline*0.7 for 5m — reduces noise for transient p99 blips
sam: agree. current alert p99>500ms for 3m was too chatty. new condition would be: p99>500ms for 5m AND decrease(tokens_processed_total[5m]) / increase(tokens_processed_total[5m]) < -0.25 (i.e. >25% drop)
carmen: can we also add a cheap query to estimate query-cardinality cost? our token-slo panels hit prom hard under long ranges. maybe use recording rules for summary metrics (region/model rollups)
mike: recording rules are the right call. create rules for: redwood_tokens_per_sec_region, redwood_request_p99_region_model (5m window)
anya: I'll draft PR for dashboard changes + runbook update. linking runbook: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/token-slo-ops — will add steps to check NAT, GPU queue, and prefix cache hit rates
luke: operational note — for apac we have smaller NAT pool sizes; ops already planning NAT scale during peak windows. we should document nat pool thresholds in runbook (connections_per_nat > 400 => scale)
oncall-bot: runbook updated: token-slo-ops (edited by anya)
sam: next actions summary: 1) anya to PR dashboard drilldown + tweak alert expression 2) mike to add recording rules + prom job for rollups 3) luke to confirm NAT pool autoscale thresholds and add to runbook 4) carmen monitor for 24h and close thread if stable
carmen: on it, I'll mute the page for minor regressions for the next 12h after we deploy the alert change (to prevent duplicates) :thumbsup:
sam: thanks team — will follow up with a short postmortem if this reoccurs.
